A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 24-page AR-AT paper, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical research content; visible differences are confined to the first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v3 reports original AR-AT experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Imagenette, alongside component ablations, representation analyses and computational timings.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the authors' AR-AT evaluations in Tables 3–4 and additional experiments throughout the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same stop-gradient operation, predictor MLP, split-BN, automatic loss balancing and multilayer regularization. The Asym-TRADES adaptation in Appendix D is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Imagenette with the same task coverage, including the L2-bounded adversarial evaluation in Appendix B.4.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments, including Tables 3–4, the broader defense comparisons in Appendix B and the Asym-TRADES comparisons in Appendix D.

E3.justification: The architectures, dataset sizes, augmentation, training budgets, attack settings and evaluation metrics in Section 4 and the appendices are identical. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The component ablations, layer and regularization-strength studies, representation analyses, batch-size tests and BN-statistics analyses are unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices B and D–F.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains mean and standard deviation reporting over five runs for LBGAT and AR-AT. Other uncertainty displays, including the timing variability in Table 19, are also identical.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative findings match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 3 retains AR-AT's 87.82% clean and 49.02% AutoAttack accuracy on CIFAR-10 with ResNet-18.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss equations and reasoning in Sections 2–3 and Appendices C and F.2 are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about gradient conflict, mixture distributions, AR-AT's effectiveness and explanations of knowledge-distillation-based defenses.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including uncertainty about layer selection and applicability to architectures without BatchNorm, such as Transformers.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, hardware, training-time information and baseline implementation links are unchanged. Both versions retain the statement that code will be made available upon publication.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are identical, including the comparisons with TRADES, LBGAT and ARREST and connections to self-supervised learning and prior split-BN approaches.

P1.justification: The first-page margin identifier changes from v3 dated 23 Jan 2025 to v4 dated 28 Aug 2025. The paper's prose, terminology, headings and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The updated first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly repositioned. All figures, tables, captions and the remaining page layout are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the same scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility information, including Appendices A–G. Changes to the arXiv stamp, its hyperlink and PDF metadata have no meaningful effect on the paper's clarity, rigor or overall quality.
